questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather and the quality of the education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The communication from Pharmaschool have been very poor from the beginning. The rules for which units we were allowed to enrole in changed after our enrolment, and there wasen't really any help or communication about this, so most of us were forced to change unites of study after the semester was started.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
At KU, not easy at all. 

A lot of emails from USYD made it overwhelming, but all information was in the emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Meetings with coordinator,  welcome activities, emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky, but gennerally it has been hard for all of us.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: live as near as possible, it makes it much more fun. If you don't it is a half day journey with terrible public transportation. Sadly no biking.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We got an email in the middle of the night (because Australia is +10hours) and everything was full the morning after. We did not know the date the mail would come, so it was impossible to plan being awake.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got a mail with all the information, and then we had to log in to their website and select our desired units of study.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: email to the coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got only one of my units, because Pharmaschool changed their rules.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instructions, then you will be fine

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been very demotivating to talk to other danish student who were allowed to have units that were more about getting to know the australian culture. All students from Pharmaschool were strictly advised to chooses from a list of six units, where USYD didn't allow enrolement in two of them. that left us with four units... Disappointing to travel to the other side of the world and not have the ability to get to know the culture.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was alright. My supervisor for my bachelor project expected me to be in the lab a lot more than other supervisors, and therefore I experienced trouble keeping up with my two other unites of study. This made my study very stressfull.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was much the same. Lectures, lab work, in class tutorials, lab reports.. 
The big  difference is that you hav to get a overall 50% mark for your work through the semester and not just in your exam to pass the unit of study. The exam is usually worth 40-60% of your grade where it in Denmark is 100%.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PCOL3011, PCOL3012, PHAR4815

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: non of those. I have heard good things about EDUH4058: Sport and Learning in Australian Culture and EDUH4052: Laerning in Outdoor Education.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did competetive cheerleading at USYD uni sport and had so much fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Everything you can imagine. 
Look it up in the USU app and Sydney uni sports

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some sport you have never tried before. You will meet new people, and have fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on surf camp, take the train to blue mountains, new castle, Jervis bay, Brisbane, Hunter vally, fly to Fiji, Uluru, go diving.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join the clubs. people are not coming to class anyway.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not going to class. people talk a lot to each other but it is very superficial.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: saying thank you to the bus driver

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join the clubs! 
Everything seems chaotic and overwhelming, but you will figure it out. 

When the exam season hits you and you realize that you should have been going to lectures instead of adventures, remember you have made it through a whole semester on your own. Be proud!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask about everything. they will help you and you are not alone.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience the homesickness, and going home to the people you love.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Academic stress.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would have been great if the our bachelor supervisors were informed equally. Some pharmacy students had 3 lab days on a semester and started their project in april while other was in the lab 2-4 days a week all 13 weeks of the semester. Both parts felt like we were missing out, and the workload was overwhelming.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
